meta.description: State individual income tax parameters for tax year 2026, 50 states plus DC. Base data: Tax Foundation table as of 2026-02-11, then updated for laws enacted later in 2026 with retroactive effect (AR, AZ, GA, SC, UT, WV) and for state-published 2026 inflation adjustments (CA, MA, ME, VT, ND, HI). Independently verified 2026-11-17 against state primary sources; that pass corrected the AZ and MD standard deductions (2025 amounts had been carried into 2026).

units.over: USD of state taxable income; marginal rate applies to income above this amount
units.property_tax_effective_rate: fraction of home value per year, owner-occupied housing, calendar 2024 (ACS)
units.sales_tax_combined_rate: state rate plus population-weighted average local rate, as of 2026-07-01

field_notes.brackets: Sorted ascending. A leading {over:0, rate:0} entry is an explicit zero bracket. Empty list means no tax on ordinary income.
field_notes.inflation_indexed: True when bracket thresholds are indexed annually by statute. Flat-rate states with no thresholds are false.
field_notes.standard_deduction.type: 'deduction', 'credit' (Utah) or 'none'. follows_federal means the state uses the federal standard deduction ($16,100 single / $32,200 joint for 2026).
field_notes.personal_exemption.type: 'deduction' reduces taxable income; 'credit' reduces tax. dependent_type is given separately because some states mix them.
field_notes.social_security.status: 'none' = benefits not taxed; 'partial' = taxed only above an income/age test or partly; 'follows_federal' = federally taxable portion is taxed.
field_notes.retirement_distributions.taxed: 'none', 'partial' (broad exclusion; see exclusion and notes) or 'full' for traditional IRA/401(k) distributions.
field_notes.local_income_tax.statewide_avg_effective: Tax Foundation estimate of local income tax as a share of AGI (2023 data).

sources: See SOURCES-states.md for the full list and judgement calls.

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

AL.name: Alabama

retirement_distributions.notes: First $6,000 of retirement plan distributions (IRA, 401(k)) exempt at 65+.

notes: Standard deduction shown is the maximum; it phases down to $2,500 single / $5,000 joint as AGI rises above about $25,500. Federal income tax paid is deductible. Dependent exemption falls to $500 above $50,000 AGI and $300 above $100,000.

AR.name: Arkansas

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $6,000 of retirement income deductible from age 59.5.

notes: Brackets are the standard (lower-income) table, thresholds taken from the DFA 2026 withholding formula, with the top rate cut from 3.9% to 3.7% retroactive to 2026-01-01 (HB 1001 / SB 1, signed 2026-05-06). Net income above roughly $94,700-$97,800 uses a second table (2% from $0, 3.7% over $4,600 per Tax Foundation) with a bracket-adjustment bridge; that adds roughly $330 of tax and is not modelled. Same schedule for every filing status; married couples may compute tax separately on one return.

AZ.name: Arizona

retirement_distributions.notes: Some government/military pensions get an exemption of up to $2,500.

notes: HB 4168 (Laws 2026, ch. 140) updated IRC conformity to 2026-01-01 and rewrote A.R.S. 43-1041(A) to a base standard deduction of $15,750/$31,500 ($23,625 head of household), applied retroactively to tax years beginning after 2024-12-31, so $15,750/$31,500 is the tax year 2025 amount. Subsection H requires the department to adjust that base for inflation in the same manner as the federal basic standard deduction, which gives the 2026 federal amount of $16,100/$32,200 stored here (statutory derivation; the 2026 Form 140 was not yet published). Dependent credit raised from $100 to $125 (under 17) for 2026. From 2026 the standard deduction is increased by charitable contributions up to $1,000 single / $2,000 joint.

CA.name: California
notes: 2026 figures from FTB Tax News October 2026 (indexed 2026 schedules, standard deduction, exemption credits). Rates include the 1% Mental Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000 (threshold not indexed, same for all filing statuses). Excludes 1.3% SDI payroll tax on all wages (Tax Foundation: 1.3% for the 2025/2026 table). Exemption credits phase out at high AGI.

CO.name: Colorado

social_security.notes: Federally taxable benefits fully deductible at age 65+. Ages 55-64: fully deductible if AGI <= $75,000 single / $95,000 joint (2026), otherwise deduction capped at $20,000. Under 55: follows federal.

retirement_distributions.notes: $20,000 retirement income deduction at ages 55-64, $24,000 at 65+.

local_income_tax.notes: Flat occupational privilege tax ($9.75 per month in Denver), not a percentage.

notes: Starts from federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction applies. TABOR surpluses can temporarily lower the rate.

CT.name: Connecticut

social_security.notes: Fully exempt if AGI below $75,000 single / $100,000 joint; above that no more than 25% of benefits are taxed.

retirement_distributions.notes: Pension, annuity and IRA income exempt or partly exempt below AGI of roughly $75,000 single / $100,000 joint, phasing out above.

notes: No standard deduction; personal exemption of $15,000/$24,000 phases out to zero above AGI $30,000 single / $48,000 joint and is partly replaced by a sliding personal credit. The 2% bracket phases out and high earners face benefit recapture, so the marginal schedule understates tax at high incomes.

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $12,500 of pension and qualified retirement plan income excluded at 60+.
No state income tax.

GA.name: Georgia

retirement_distributions.notes: Retirement income exclusion of $35,000 at 62-64 and $65,000 at 65+.

notes: HB 463 (2026) cut the flat rate from 5.19% to 4.99% retroactive to 2026-01-01 and raised the standard deduction to $15,000/$30,000 (rising $375/$750 a year from 2027 toward $18,000/$36,000). HB 463 also raised the dependent exemption from $4,000 to $5,000 for 2026 (rising $125 a year from 2027 toward $6,000), confirmed in the bill text. Further cuts of 0.125 points a year toward 3.99% depend on revenue triggers.

HI.name: Hawaii

retirement_distributions.notes: Employer-funded pensions exempt; 401(k) elective-deferral and IRA distributions taxable.

notes: Standard deduction for 2026 is $8,000/$16,000 under Act 46 (SLH 2024), confirmed by Hawaii DOTAX announcement 2024-03; the February 2026 Tax Foundation table still showed $4,400/$8,800. Brackets same as 2025. Act 24 (2026) adds a 13% rate over $1,000,000 from 2027.

retirement_distributions.notes: Retirement income exempt from age 55; taxable before 55.

ID.name: Idaho
notes: Flat 5.3% above a zero bracket. Zero-bracket threshold shown is the 2025 amount ($4,811 single / $9,622 joint); it is indexed annually and the 2026 amount had not been published.

IL.name: Illinois

retirement_distributions.notes: Qualified retirement plan, IRA and pension income fully exempt.

notes: Personal exemption unavailable above AGI $250,000 single / $500,000 joint.

KS.name: Kansas

retirement_distributions.notes: Public pensions exempt.

local_income_tax.notes: Local intangibles tax on interest and dividends in some jurisdictions only.

notes: Personal exemption $9,160 single / $18,320 joint plus $2,320 per dependent.

KY.name: Kentucky

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $31,110 per person of pension/retirement distributions excluded.

local_income_tax.notes: Occupational licence taxes on wages; school district add-ons in some places.

notes: Standard deduction is per taxpayer and not doubled on a joint return.

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $12,000 excluded at 65+; public pensions exempt.

MA.name: Massachusetts

retirement_distributions.notes: Government pensions may be exempt.

notes: 4% surtax threshold for 2026 is $1,107,750 (indexed annually); the 5% base rate has no brackets. Excludes PFML payroll contribution.

MD.name: Maryland

retirement_distributions.notes: Pension exclusion up to $40,600 at 65+; 401(k)/IRA distributions otherwise taxable.

long_term_capital_gains.notes: Additional 2% on capital gains when federal AGI exceeds $350,000.

local_income_tax.notes: Counties and Baltimore City levy local income taxes; statewide average about 2.4% of AGI.

notes: Brackets shown are state only; every county and Baltimore City add a local income tax. Personal exemption phases out above AGI $100,000 single / $150,000 joint.

Standard deduction: $3,350/$6,700 was the tax year 2025 amount. Tax-General 10-217(c) indexes it for tax years after 2025 by the IRC 1(f)(3) cost-of-living adjustment (base year 2024), with the increase rounded down to a multiple of $50. The Comptroller's 2026 withholding guide gives $3,400 for single; the joint amount of $6,850 is computed from the same rule (6,700 x about 2.27% = $152, rounded down to $150) and was not yet printed on a 2026 Form 502.

ME.name: Maine

retirement_distributions.notes: Pension income deduction up to $48,216; federal pensions exempt.

notes: From Maine Revenue Services 2026 Individual Income Tax Rates (revised 2026-05-20). Top bracket includes the new 2% surcharge on taxable income over $1,000,000 single / $1,500,000 joint, effective 2026. Standard deduction and personal exemption phase out at high income. Dependent amount is a $305 credit (2025 amount).

retirement_distributions.notes: Retirement and pension income (pensions, IRA distributions) largely exempt from tax year 2026 (PA 4 of 2023, PA 24 of 2025).

MN.name: Minnesota

social_security.notes: Federally taxable benefits fully subtracted if AGI below $84,490 single / $108,320 joint (2026); subtraction falls 10% for each $4,000 above.

notes: Standard deduction is reduced for AGI above about $244,400. Additional 1% tax on net investment income over $1,000,000.

MO.name: Missouri

retirement_distributions.notes: Public pension exemption and a limited private pension deduction.

long_term_capital_gains.notes: Capital gains exempt from individual income tax from 2025.

notes: Federal income tax paid is partly deductible. Standard deduction equals the federal amount.

retirement_distributions.notes: Qualified retirement income exempt; early withdrawals taxable.

MT.name: Montana

social_security.notes: Federally taxable benefits are taxed; taxpayers 65+ get a $5,500 subtraction from income.

retirement_distributions.notes: $5,500 subtraction at 65+.

long_term_capital_gains.notes: Separate lower rate schedule for net long-term gains (top 4.1%).

notes: Starts from federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction applies.

ND.name: North Dakota
notes: 2026 thresholds confirmed against the Tax Rate Schedules printed on the 2026 Form ND-1ES (single $49,575/$250,400; joint $82,800/$304,850); they are the 2025 thresholds ($48,475/$244,825 single, $80,975/$298,075 joint) indexed by about 2.27%.

retirement_distributions.notes: Military retirement exempt.

NH.name: New Hampshire

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

notes: Interest and dividends tax fully repealed for tax years beginning after 2024; no individual income tax in 2026.

retirement_distributions.notes: At 62+: exclusion up to $75,000 single / $100,000 joint, phased out as income rises to $150,000.

local_income_tax.notes: Employer payroll tax, not paid by individuals.

NM.name: New Mexico

social_security.notes: Exempt if income <= $100,000 single / $150,000 joint; otherwise follows federal.

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $8,000 deduction at 65+, income-limited.

long_term_capital_gains.notes: Greater of $2,500 or 40% of gain (up to $1,000,000) from sale of a New Mexico business; ordinary portfolio gains get only the $2,500.

notes: The $4,000 dependent deduction applies to all but one dependent.

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

NY.name: New York

retirement_distributions.notes: $20,000 pension and annuity exclusion from age 59.5; federal, NY state/local and military pensions exempt.

local_income_tax.notes: NYC resident income tax is graduated; 3.876% is the top rate.

notes: Tax-benefit recapture makes high-income taxpayers pay the top applicable rate on all income. Dependent exemption $1,000.

OH.name: Ohio

retirement_distributions.notes: Military retirement pay exempt.

local_income_tax.notes: Most cities and many school districts levy income taxes.

notes: Flat 2.75% on nonbusiness income above $26,050 from 2026 (HB 96). Personal exemption is $2,400 at AGI <= $40,000, $2,150 to $80,000, $1,900 above, and unavailable above $500,000.

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $10,000 per person of retirement income exempt.

OR.name: Oregon

local_income_tax.notes: 4% is the combined top rate of the 1% regional (Metro) and 3% Multnomah County taxes, which apply only above income thresholds.

notes: Federal income tax paid is deductible up to a cap. Personal exemption credit unavailable above federal AGI $100,000 single / $200,000 joint.

retirement_distributions.notes: Traditional retirement income (pensions, 401(k), IRA) is not taxed.

local_income_tax.notes: Philadelphia wage tax rate is the 2023 resident rate; most municipalities levy an earned income tax of about 1%.

RI.name: Rhode Island

social_security.notes: Exempt for those at full retirement age with federal AGI below $107,000 single / $133,750 joint; otherwise follows federal.

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $50,000 of pension/annuity/401(k) income exempt at full retirement age, income-limited; IRA distributions taxable.

notes: Standard deduction and exemptions phase out between modified federal AGI of about $261,000 and $290,800.

SC.name: South Carolina

phase_out.method: linear to zero across the range

retirement_distributions.notes: Retirement income exclusion of up to $15,000; existing deductions retained under H. 4216.

notes: H. 4216 (signed 2026-03-30) replaced the 0%/3%/6% schedule for tax year 2026: 1.99% up to $30,000 and 5.21% above (SCDOR states it as 5.21% minus $966). Federal standard/itemized deductions are replaced by the SC Income Adjusted Deduction ($15,000 single, $22,500 HoH, $30,000 joint) which phases out proportionally over federal AGI $40,000-$95,000 single / $80,000-$190,000 joint. Other SC deductions (dependent exemption, retirement and age-65 deductions, 44% capital gains deduction) are retained. Indexation of the new brackets is not confirmed (set false). The 5.21% rate falls in later years if revenue-growth triggers are met.

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

TN.name: Tennessee

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

notes: Hall tax on interest and dividends fully repealed in 2021.

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

UT.name: Utah

social_security.notes: Follows federal, offset by a non-refundable Social Security benefits credit that phases out with income (thresholds not captured here).

retirement_distributions.notes: Retirement credit of up to $450, income-limited.

notes: SB 60 (2026) cut the flat rate from 4.5% to 4.45% retroactive to 2026-01-01. In place of a standard deduction Utah gives a non-refundable taxpayer credit of 6% of the federal standard/itemized deduction plus personal exemptions ($966/$1,932 at the 2026 federal standard deduction), phasing out at 1.3 cents per dollar of income above about $18,213 single / $36,426 joint (2025 thresholds). Dependent exemption amount ($2,111) feeds that credit and is a 2025 figure.

retirement_distributions.notes: Age deduction up to $12,000 at 65+, reduced above AGI $50,000 single / $75,000 joint.

VT.name: Vermont

social_security.notes: Full exemption if AGI <= $50,000 single / $65,000 joint, phasing out completely at $60,000 / $75,000; otherwise follows federal.

retirement_distributions.notes: Limited exemption for some government pensions.

notes: 2026 bracket widths are derived from the Vermont Department of Taxes 2026 percentage-method withholding tables (annual table minus the built-in zero bracket) and match the 2025 schedule indexed by about 2.7%; the $5,400 exemption is the 2026 withholding allowance. The $7,850/$15,700 standard deduction is the 2025 amount ($7,650/$15,300) indexed the same way and matches one secondary source; not confirmed against the 2026 rate schedule, which was not yet published. Taxpayers with federal AGI over $150,000 pay at least 3% of AGI.

WA.name: Washington

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.

long_term_capital_gains.notes: 7% excise on long-term capital gains above the standard deduction ($278,000 for 2025, indexed; 2026 amount not published) and 9.9% on taxable gains above $1,000,000. Some asset types are excluded. The deduction is per individual or married couple (not doubled for couples).

notes: No tax on wages or ordinary income. 7% excise on long-term capital gains above the standard deduction and 9.9% on gains above $1,000,000 (see long_term_capital_gains). 0.58% WA Cares payroll premium on wages is not included. A 9.9% tax on income above $1,000,000 was enacted in 2026 to take effect in 2028.

WI.name: Wisconsin

retirement_distributions.notes: Up to $24,000 per person excludable at 67+ for some retirees (income-limited).

notes: Standard deduction phases out with income (starts about $20,119 single / $29,039 joint, zero at about $136,453 / $159,690).

WV.name: West Virginia

social_security.notes: Fully exempt for all incomes from tax year 2026 (phase-out of the tax completed).

retirement_distributions.notes: Pensions taxable with some exclusions.

local_income_tax.notes: Flat city service fees ($6 per pay period in Charleston), not a percentage.

notes: SB 392 (2026) cut all rates about 5% retroactive to 2026-01-01; schedule from the WV Tax Division. Same thresholds for single and joint filers.

retirement_distributions.notes: No state income tax.
Small ($3,000) exclusion for some government pensions.
